vyānaśe bhuvanam añjanācalaprasthapaṅktinibiḍaṃ niśātamaḥ //
na dvitīyam anubhūyate sma vastv antikād api tamas tiraskṛtam /
children.translated_text: Not even a second object could be experienced, even nearby, concealed by the darkness;

children.text: kevalātmaviṣayaṃ tadābhavaj jñānam ulbaparivāsinām iva //
children.translated_text: Knowledge then became solely self-referential, as if belonging to those still enclosed in the womb.

children.text: na dvitīyam anubhūyate sma vastv antikād api tamas tiraskṛtam /
kevalātmaviṣayaṃ tada ābhavaj jñānam ulbaparivāsinām iva //
dūramiśritaparasparāṅgakair apy ayogajanitajvarair iva /
children.translated_text: Even couples whose limbs were closely intertwined, as if afflicted by the fever of separation born of non-contact,

children.text: durlabhānanavilokanāmṛtair dūyate sma mithunair mitho bhṛśam //
children.translated_text: Deprived of the nectar of beholding each other's faces, suffered greatly from one another.

children.text: dūramiśritaparasparāṅgakair apy ayogajanitajvarair iva /
durlabhānanavilokanāmṛtair dūyate sma mithunair mitho bhṛśam //
so 'tiśītahimaśīkaro marun nūnam ulmukacayān avākirat /
children.translated_text: That wind, exceedingly cold with frost and snow, must have scattered embers [from the fires],

children.text: yac cukūja bhṛśam ārtikāhalaṃ cakravākayuvatis tapasvinī //
children.translated_text: For the wretched <s>cakravāka</s>-hen shrieked loudly, a cry resounding with anguish.

children.text: so 'tiśītahimaśīkaro marun nūnam ulmukacayān avākirat /
yac cukūja bhṛśam ārtikāhalaṃ cakravākayuvatis tapasvinī //
uccacāra na vanasthalīṣv asau marmaraḥ patitapatranisvanaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the forest clearings, the rustling sound of fallen leaves did not stir,

children.text: nāvirāsa karikṛṣṭasallakībhaṅgayonir asakṛc caṭatkṛtiḥ //
children.translated_text: Nor did the repeated cracking sounds born from elephants breaking <s>sallakī</s> (Indian frankincense) trees.

children.text: uccacāra na vanasthalīṣv asau marmaraḥ patitapatranisvanaḥ /
na avirāsa karikṛṣṭasallakībhaṅgayonir asakṛc caṭatkṛtiḥ //
tasthur āsthitamanuṣyamūrtayo yāmikā iva vidūrato 'drayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The mountains stood in the distance like night-watchmen who had assumed human forms;

children.text: prahvabālaviṭapāgrapāṇayas tau parītya taravaḥ siṣevire //
children.translated_text: The trees, with their bowed young branch-tips as hands, surrounded and attended upon those two [heroes].

children.text: tasthur āsthitamanuṣyamūrtayo yāmikā iva vidūrato 'drayaḥ /
prahvabālaviṭapāgrapāṇayas tau parītya taravaḥ siṣevire //
drāṅ nidāgham anudadrajo 'dhunād viślathāṃ bṛhatikām asārayat /
children.translated_text: Swiftly it drove away the lingering summer heat, loosened the clinging humidity;

children.text: pratyapadyata vanānilas tayor ekasannihitayāmikavratam //
children.translated_text: The forest breeze assumed the duty of a solitary night-watchman stationed beside them.

children.text: drāṅ nidāgham anudadrajo 'dhunād viślathāṃ bṛhatikām asārayat /
pratyapadyata vanānilas tayor ekasannihitayāmikavratam //
sānujasya tamasi pramīlatas tasya bhāvimamatāhṛtā iva /
children.translated_text: As he [<s>Rāma</s>] slept with his younger brother in the darkness, as if drawn by the affection that was destined to be,

children.text: ujjvalāyataviṣāṇasūcitāś cakrire parikaraṃ mataṅgajāḥ //
children.translated_text: Elephants, their presence announced by their bright, elongated tusks, formed a protective circle around him.

children.text: sānujasya tamasi pramīlatas tasya bhāvimamatāhṛtā iva /
ujjvalāyataviṣāṇasūcitāś cakrire parikaraṃ mataṅgajāḥ //
dīpakṛtyam akarod upāntike niṣprakamparuciroṣadhīgaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: The cluster of radiant herbs, motionless, performed the function of lamps nearby;

children.text: tenur adrivanamadhyasuptayor maṅgalāni vanadevatās tayoḥ //
children.translated_text: The forest deities extended blessings over the two as they slept amidst the mountain forests.

children.text: dīpakṛtyam akarod upāntike niṣprakamparuciroṣadhīgaṇaḥ /
tenur adrivanamadhyasuptayor maṅgalāni vanadevatās tayoḥ //
ehi jānaki bhujāntaraṃ kharaḥ prastaro 'yam asi kiṃ parāṅmukhī /
children.translated_text: "Come, <s>Jānakī</s>, into the space between my arms — this slab of stone is rough; why do you turn away?

children.text: matkapolam upadhāya supyatām aprasaktir iyatī kadā nu te //
children.translated_text: Rest your head upon my cheek and sleep — when has such indifference ever been yours?

children.text: ehi jānaki bhujāntaraṃ kharaḥ prastaro 'yam asi kiṃ parāṅmukhī /
matkapolam upadhāya supyatām aprasaktir iyatī kadā nu te //
kṣiptam aṃśukam idaṃ mayorasi prīyatāṃ tava nirānandaḥ stanaḥ /
children.translated_text: "This garment of mine has been cast upon your bosom; let your joyless breast find delight;

children.text: nīvinodini kare kuru kṣamām āyatākṣi nudasīva kiṃ punaḥ //
children.translated_text: O loosener of girdle-knots, place your hand in patience, O large-eyed one — why do you push me away?"

children.text: kṣiptam aṃśukam idaṃ maya ūrasi prīyatāṃ tava nirānandaḥ stanaḥ /
nīvinodini kare kuru kṣamām āyatākṣi nudasi iva kiṃ punaḥ //
suptavākyam iti maithilīpater maithilīvirahadūyamānayā /
children.translated_text: These sleep-words of the lord of <s>Maithilī</s>, tormented by separation from <s>Maithilī</s>,

children.text: diksakhīnivahavāritāsrayā śuśruve vasudhayopasannayā //
children.translated_text: Were heard by the Earth, who had drawn near, her tears being held back by her companions the directions.

children.text: suptavākyam iti maithilīpater maithilīvirahadūyamānayā /
diksakhīnivahavāritāsrayā śuśruve vasudhaya ūpasannayā //
mad bibheti virahī raghūdvaho mad vinā ca na jagat pramodate /
children.translated_text: "The hero of <s>Raghu</s>'s line fears me in separation, and without me the world takes no delight;

children.text: tat karomi kim itīva cintayan nojjagāma sahasā niśākaraḥ //
children.translated_text: What then shall I do?" — as if pondering thus, the moon did not suddenly rise.

children.text: mad bibheti virahī raghūdvaho mad vinā ca na jagat pramodate /
tat karomi kim iti iva cintayan na ujjagāma sahasā niśākaraḥ //
na sma bhāti kim api sphuṭaṃ puraḥ kiṃcid īritakareṇa kevalam /
children.translated_text: Nothing at all was clearly visible ahead; only with a slightly extended hand

children.text: dṛśyate sma divi dūravartinā tarjyamānam iva kenacit tamaḥ //
children.translated_text: Could one see, as if something far away in the sky were threatening the darkness.

children.text: na sma bhāti kim api sphuṭaṃ puraḥ kiṃcid īritakareṇa kevalam /
dṛśyate sma divi dūravartinā tarjyamānam iva kenacit tamaḥ //
jāyate sma ghanamālatīguṇaśreṇigarbhakabarīmanoharam /
children.translated_text: There appeared a darkness that was beautiful with the tresses intertwined with strands of dense jasmine garlands,

children.text: meghavāhanadigaṅganāmukhe mugdhacandrakarakarburaṃ tamaḥ //
children.translated_text: Mottled with soft moonbeams upon the face of the celestial maiden of the cloud-bearing direction [the northeast].

children.text: jāyate sma ghanamālatīguṇaśreṇigarbhakabarīmanoharam /
meghavāhanadigaṅganāmukhe mugdhacandrakarakarburaṃ tamaḥ //
sānurāgam upagūḍham agrimair aṃśubhiḥ śaśabhṛto davīyasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Embraced with affection by the foremost rays of the moon still far away,

children.text: unnanāma namucidviṣo diśi srastastaṃtamasabhāram ambaram //
children.translated_text: The sky, its burden of dense darkness slipping off, rose up in the direction of <s>Indra</s> (the east).

children.text: sānurāgam upagūḍham agrimair aṃśubhiḥ śaśabhṛto davīyasaḥ /
unnanāma namucidviṣo diśi srastastaṃtamasabhāram ambaram //
ujjvalāgrakiraṇapraveśakaproktasatvarasamāgamo 'pi san /
children.translated_text: Though its swift approach had been announced by the entry of its bright leading rays,

children.text: prekṣyate sma janitotsukaś cirād vyomaraṅgamukhasaṃmukhaḥ śaśī //
children.translated_text: The moon, having long generated eagerness, was seen facing the stage of the sky.

children.text: ujjvalāgrakiraṇapraveśakaproktasatvarasamāgamo 'pi san /
prekṣyate sma janitotsukaś cirād vyomaraṅgamukhasaṃmukhaḥ śaśī //
audayena śaśino gabhastinā bhinnaśeṣatimiraṃ vyarājata /
children.translated_text: By the rising ray of the moon, the remaining darkness was split, and it shone forth —

children.text: mṛjyamānam iva śakradiṅmukhaṃ kuṅkumena mṛganābhoyogin //
children.translated_text: The face of <s>Indra</s>'s direction appeared as if being anointed with saffron mixed with musk.

children.text: audayena śaśino gabhastinā bhinnaśeṣatimiraṃ vyarājata /
mṛjyamānam iva śakradiṅmukhaṃ kuṅkumena mṛganābhoyogin //
taṃ babhāra na vidhur navodayaṃ kiṃ tu kuṅkumavilepanāruṇam /
children.translated_text: The moon did not bear that [light] as a new rising, but rather as a red saffron ointment —

children.text: ekam utsukavaśāt payodharaṃ vyācakāra haridigvilāsinī //
children.translated_text: The enchantress of the eastern direction revealed a single breast, out of eagerness.

children.text: taṃ babhāra na vidhur navodayaṃ kiṃ tu kuṅkumavilepanāruṇam /
ekam utsukavaśāt payodharaṃ vyācakāra haridigvilāsinī //
āttajaitranijapuṣpadhanvano manmathasya bhuvanāni jeṣyataḥ /
children.translated_text: Of <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love), who had taken up his own victorious flower-bow to conquer the worlds,

children.text: unnanāma purataḥ śaśicchalāt pūrṇarukmakalaśaḥ payonidheḥ //
children.translated_text: There rose before him, under the pretext of the moon, the full golden vessel from the ocean.

children.text: āttajaitranijapuṣpadhanvano manmathasya bhuvanāni jeṣyataḥ /
unnanāma purataḥ śaśicchalāt pūrṇarukmakalaśaḥ payonidheḥ //
diksarāgamukhasannidhāpitasphītacandracaṣakā śatakratoḥ /
children.translated_text: The direction of <s>Śatakratu</s> (<s>Indra</s>), bearing the abundant moon-cup placed near its flushed countenance,

children.text: kṣībabhāvam iva bibhratī babhau viślathācchatimirāṃśukoccayā //
children.translated_text: Shone as if displaying intoxication, its dense garment of darkness loosened and slipping.

children.text: diksarāgamukhasannidhāpitasphītacandracaṣakā śatakratoḥ /
kṣībabhāvam iva bibhratī babhau viślathācchatimirāṃśukoccayā //
nandayan bhuvanam unmukhaṃ cirān mandayan smaraviruddham udyamam /
children.translated_text: Delighting the world that had long been upturned [in expectation], weakening the effort hostile to <s>Smara</s> (the god of love),

children.text: krandayan virahiṇo vihaṅgamān sāndrayan pramadam indur udyayau //
children.translated_text: Making the separated birds cry, intensifying joy — the moon rose.

children.text: nandayan bhuvanam unmukhaṃ cirān mandayan smaraviruddham udyamam /
krandayan virahiṇo vihaṅgamān sāndrayan pramadam indur udyayau //
locanālinivahaikapaṅkajaṃ cittahaṃsaśayanīyasaikatam /
children.translated_text: The single lotus for the bee-rows of eyes, the sandbank that serves as the bed for the swan of the mind,

children.text: ujjagāma ratikelimandiraṃ yāminīyuvatijīvitaṃ śaśī //
children.translated_text: The temple of amorous sport, the very life of the maiden Night — the moon arose.

children.text: locanālinivahaikapaṅkajaṃ cittahaṃsaśayanīyasaikatam /
ujjagāma ratikelimandiraṃ yāminīyuvatijīvitaṃ śaśī //
āliliṅga rajanīm ahāsayad bidyamānamukulāṃ kumudvatīm /
children.translated_text: He embraced the night, made the water-lily beds laugh as their buds split open,

children.text: agrahīd uḍuvadhūkarān karair dyāṃ prasādam anayat samaṃ śasśī //
children.translated_text: Took the hands of the star-maidens in his own rays, and bestowed grace upon the sky — the moon, all at once.

children.text: āliliṅga rajanīm ahāsayad bidyamānamukulāṃ kumudvatīm /
agrahīd uḍuvadhūkarān karair dyāṃ prasādam anayat samaṃ śasśī //
ādade viyad alāñchanavrataṃ lāñchanaṃ nijam agūhad aṃśubhiḥ /
children.translated_text: He took possession of the sky as his own spotless domain, concealed his own spot with his rays,

children.text: prāhiṇod apasṛtāsu kaumudīṃ dikṣu dakṣatanayāparigrahī //
children.translated_text: And sent forth moonlight to the departing directions — he, the son of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s daughter's husband [i.e., the moon, grandson of <s>Dakṣa</s>].

children.text: ādade viyad alāñchanavrataṃ lāñchanaṃ nijam agūhad aṃśubhiḥ /
prāhiṇod apasṛtāsu kaumudīṃ dikṣu dakṣatanayāparigrahī //
vyāpya dūram atha nirmalaṃ viyad vītapaṅkam iva paṅkajākaram /
children.translated_text: Then, pervading the clear sky far and wide — like a lotus pond freed of mud —

children.text: rejur agrakiraṇāḥ kṣapāpateḥ pūtakokanadakandakomalāḥ //
children.translated_text: The leading rays of the lord of the night shone, tender as the stamens of pure red lotuses.

children.text: vyāpya dūram atha nirmalaṃ viyad vītapaṅkam iva paṅkajākaram /
rejur agrakiraṇāḥ kṣapāpateḥ pūtakokanadakandakomalāḥ //
khe kakupsu bhuvi ca kṣapāpateḥ petur ūḍhanicayā marīcayaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the sky, in the directions, and upon the earth, the massed rays of the lord of night fell;

children.text: yatra tatra kuharāṇi kānicit kampamānam aviśan niśātamaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here and there, the remaining night-darkness, trembling, entered certain hollows.

children.text: khe kakupsu bhuvi ca kṣapāpateḥ petur ūḍhanicayā marīcayaḥ /
yatra tatra kuharāṇi kānicit kampamānam aviśan niśātamaḥ //
kṣiptam indurucibhir vyalambata tryambakasya śikhinaś ca diṅmukhe /
children.translated_text: Cast by the moon's rays, [darkness] hung at the edge of the direction of <s>Tryambaka</s> (<s>Śiva</s>, the north) and the direction of <s>Śikhin</s> (<s>Agni</s>, the southeast);

children.text: tatra nunnam anubandhaniḥsahaṃ kāndiśīkam iva niṣṭhitaṃ tamaḥ //
children.translated_text: There, surely, the darkness had settled, as if fleeing in panic, unable to bear the pursuit.

children.text: kṣiptam indurucibhir vyalambata tryambakasya śikhinaś ca diṅmukhe /
tatra nunnam anubandhaniḥsahaṃ kāndiśīkam iva niṣṭhitaṃ tamaḥ //
kandarāṇi ca mahāmahībhṛtāṃ koṭarāṇi ca jaranmahīruhām /
children.translated_text: In the caverns of great mountains, in the hollows of ancient trees,

children.text: adhyuvāsa kamalodarāṇi ca dhvāntam adhvagavadhūmukhāni ca //
children.translated_text: In the cups of lotuses, and upon the faces of travellers' wives — there the darkness took up residence.

children.text: kandarāṇi ca mahāmahībhṛtāṃ koṭarāṇi ca jaranmahīruhām /
adhyuvāsa kamalodarāṇi ca dhvāntam adhvagavadhūmukhāni ca //
svīcakāra karakoṭilālanālambitoḍutatimekhalāṃ divam /
children.translated_text: The moon claimed the sky, which wore a girdle of star-clusters dangling from its fingertip-caresses,

children.text: rāgabhaṅgam atisaṃstavād gatāṃ devarājadiśam indur atyajat //
children.translated_text: And abandoned the direction of <s>Devarāja</s> (<s>Indra</s>, the east), which had lost its blush from excessive intimacy.

children.text: svīcakāra karakoṭilālanālambitoḍutatimekhalāṃ divam /
rāgabhaṅgam atisaṃstavād gatāṃ devarājadiśam indur atyajat //
ātatāna gaganāṅgaṇādhikair medinīm amṛtavarṣibhir vidhuḥ /
children.translated_text: The moon spread over the earth, from rays that exceeded the sky's expanse,

children.text: viprayuktajanadhūmaketubhiḥ ketakāgraśucibhir marīcibhiḥ //
children.translated_text: That rained nectar, that were pure as the tips of <s>ketaka</s> (screwpine) flowers — rays that were comets of anguish for the separated.

children.text: ātatāna gaganāṅgaṇādhikair medinīm amṛtavarṣibhir vidhuḥ /
viprayuktajanadhūmaketubhiḥ ketakāgraśucibhir marīcibhiḥ //
saṃkucadbhir abhirāmatādhike sādhu candramasi puṣkaraiḥ kṛtam /
children.translated_text: By the lotuses, which contracted when the beauty of the moon excelled, it was well done;

children.text: udyatā jayini kāminīmukhe tena sāhasam anuṣṭhitaṃ punaḥ //
children.translated_text: But then, by that [moon], risen and victorious, yet another audacity was committed against the faces of lovely women.

children.text: saṃkucadbhir abhirāmatādhike sādhu candramasi puṣkaraiḥ kṛtam /
udyatā jayini kāminīmukhe tena sāhasam anuṣṭhitaṃ punaḥ //
uccakhāna ruṣam uccamaṇḍalaḥ khaṇḍanām agamayad viṣahyatām /
children.translated_text: Rising to full orb, the lord of night excavated anger, brought endurance to those who had been slighted,

children.text: mānapaṅkam apanīya kāminīḥ kāntahastam anayan niśāpatiḥ //
children.translated_text: Removed the mud of pride from women, and led them to their lovers' hands.

children.text: uccakhāna ruṣam uccamaṇḍalaḥ khaṇḍanām agamayad viṣahyatām /
mānapaṅkam apanīya kāminīḥ kāntahastam anayan niśāpatiḥ //
vyaktavartmabilavāhinīvanagrāmagulmagahanādribhedayā /
children.translated_text: With the moonlight's distinct delineation of paths, water-channels, forests, villages, thickets, dense groves, and mountain-clefts,

children.text: saumyatādhikaviśeṣayājani jyotsnayā divasaniḥspṛho janaḥ //
children.translated_text: People became indifferent to daylight, so surpassing was the gentleness [of the scene].

children.text: vyaktavartmabilavāhinīvanagrāmagulmagahanādribhedayā /
saumyatādhikaviśeṣaya ājani jyotsnayā divasaniḥspṛho janaḥ //
pīyate sma kumudaṃ na locanaiś candrikā tapati rohitacchadam /
children.translated_text: The eyes did not drink in the night-lily; the moonlight scorched the red lotus;

children.text: prādurāsa param utpibann aliḥ saurabhaṃ niravalambam ambuni //
children.translated_text: But a bee emerged, drinking in the fragrance that floated unsupported upon the water.

children.text: pīyate sma kumudaṃ na locanaiś candrikā tapati rohitacchadam /
prādurāsa param utpibann aliḥ saurabhaṃ niravalambam ambuni //
ekikeva nijavṛndamadhyagāpy uccukūja sabhayā sitacchadī /
children.translated_text: A white goose, though amidst her own flock, cried out alone in fear;

children.text: dantamūlam asakṛc ca saṃśayād āmamarśa kariṇaḥ kareṇukā //
children.translated_text: And a she-elephant, out of doubt, repeatedly felt the base of the tusks of the bull elephant beside her.

children.text: ekika īva nijavṛndamadhyaga āpy uccukūja sabhayā sitacchadī /
dantamūlam asakṛc ca saṃśayād āmamarśa kariṇaḥ kareṇukā //
ketakīṣu kadalīṣu vālukāsv aśmasu sphuṭitakairave 'mbhasi /
children.translated_text: Upon <s>ketakī</s> flowers, upon plantain trees, upon sandy banks, upon stones, upon blooming night-lilies in the water —

children.text: lambhiteva laharīparamparām ullalāsa śaśikāntivāhinī //
children.translated_text: The stream of moonlight, as if generating wave upon wave, shimmered and danced.

children.text: ketakīṣu kadalīṣu vālukāsv aśmasu sphuṭitakairave 'mbhasi /
lambhita īva laharīparamparām ullalāsa śaśikāntivāhinī //
prāptasūkṣmaghanapallavāntaraiś citritāḥ śaśikarair itas tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Dappled here and there by moonbeams that had penetrated the interstices of fine, dense foliage,

children.text: bibhrati sma tarumūlaśāyinaḥ śambarāḥ pṛṣatayūthavibhramam //
children.translated_text: The deer sleeping at the roots of trees bore the semblance of herds of spotted antelope.

children.text: prāptasūkṣmaghanapallavāntaraiś citritāḥ śaśikarair itas tataḥ /
bibhrati sma tarumūlaśāyinaḥ śambarāḥ pṛṣatayūthavibhramam //
kṛcchralabdhanagaśṛṅgasandhayo dattamanmathajayābhisandhayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The moonbeams, having with difficulty found the junctions of mountain-peaks, delivering the resolve of <s>Manmatha</s>'s (the god of love's) victory,

children.text: maithilītaravadhūdurāsadaṃ rāghavāṅkam aviśac chaśitviṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: Entered the lap of <s>Rāghava</s> (<s>Rāma</s>), inaccessible to any woman other than <s>Maithilī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>).

children.text: kṛcchralabdhanagaśṛṅgasandhayo dattamanmathajayābhisandhayaḥ /
maithilītaravadhūdurāsadaṃ rāghavāṅkam aviśac chaśitviṣaḥ //
jāgarṣi kāśmari niṣīdasi kovidāra kutrāsi vatsa kṛtamāla tamāla paśya /
children.translated_text: "Are you awake, O <s>kāśmarī</s> tree? Are you sitting up, O <s>kovidāra</s>? Where are you, dear <s>kṛtamāla</s>? Look, O <s>tamāla</s>!

children.text: kiṃ vartate raghupater iti satvarābhir uktaṃ drumaugham avalokya vanasthalībhiḥ //
children.translated_text: What is happening with the lord of <s>Raghu</s>'s line?" — so the forest-glades seemed to say in haste, surveying the host of trees.

children.text: jāgarṣi kāśmari niṣīdasi kovidāra kutra asi vatsa kṛtamāla tamāla paśya /
kiṃ vartate raghupater iti satvarābhir uktaṃ drumaugham avalokya vanasthalībhiḥ //
anyonyadūrapariṣaktaviśālasāndraśākhāśatais tarubhir antarayāṃbabhūve /
children.translated_text: By the trees, whose vast and dense hundreds of branches were clasped to one another from afar, the moonlight was obstructed —

children.text: udbhūtaghoravirahajvaralaṅghitasya candrātapaḥ sa khalu dāśarather apathyaḥ //
children.translated_text: That moonlight, which was indeed unwholesome for the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, who was overleaping [all bounds] with the terrible fever of separation.

children.text: anyonyadūrapariṣaktaviśālasāndraśākhāśatais tarubhir antarayāṃbabhūve /
udbhūtaghoravirahajvaralaṅghitasya candrātapaḥ sa khalu dāśarather apathyaḥ //
kumudavanam ahetu tyaktanidraṃ tadāsīd gaganam uḍuvitānair dhig vṛthaiva praphullam /
children.translated_text: The night-lily garden, without cause, had abandoned sleep; the sky was uselessly bedecked with canopies of stars — alas;

children.text: ajani jagad adhīśasyāgṛhītes tadānīṃ vidhur api vidhavastrīyauvanodbhedaśocyaḥ //
children.translated_text: For the lord of the world [<s>Rāma</s>] had not taken [<s>Sītā</s>] — and so the moon too became pitiable, like the burgeoning youth of a widowed woman.

children.text: kumudavanam ahetu tyaktanidraṃ tadā āsīd gaganam uḍuvitānair dhig vṛtha aiva praphullam /
ajani jagad adhīśasya agṛhītes tadānīṃ vidhur api vidhavastrīyauvanodbhedaśocyaḥ //
śvasiti janakaputrī satvaro bhānuputraḥ kapipatir upasannaṃ suprabhātaṃ taveti /
children.translated_text: "The daughter of <s>Janaka</s> sighs; the swift son of the Sun [<s>Sugrīva</s>]; the lord of monkeys [<s>Sugrīva</s>] is near — may you have a good morning" —

children.text: jagur iva raghunāthāyārdhabuddhāḥ svananto madhuram apararātre patriṇaḥ ke 'pi ke 'pi //
children.translated_text: Thus, as if singing to the lord of <s>Raghu</s>'s line, some birds, half-awakened, called sweetly in the last watch of the night.

children.text: śvasiti janakaputrī satvaro bhānuputraḥ kapipatir upasannaṃ suprabhātaṃ tava iti /
jagur iva raghunāthāya ardhabuddhāḥ svananto madhuram apararātre patriṇaḥ ke 'pi ke 'pi //
ity abhinandakṛtau rāmacarite mahākāvye sandhyātamaścandrodayavarṇano nāma dvitīyaḥ sargaḥ samāptaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Rāmacarita Mahākāvya</s> composed by <s>Abhinanda</s>, the second canto named "Description of Twilight, Darkness, and Moonrise" is concluded.

children.text: kavīnāṃ kiṃ dattair nṛpapaśubhir anyair avasare paraṃ pṛthvīpālaḥ kṣaṇam api sa karṇo vitaratu /
children.translated_text: What has been given by other kings, who are mere beasts? Let that supreme king <s>Karṇa</s> bestow but a moment [of his attention];

children.text: anāttaṃ tattvajñair api suvipulārthavyayabhiyā pratiṣṭhāṃ yenoccair jagati gamitaṃ rāmacaritam //
children.translated_text: By whom the <s>Rāmacarita</s>, which even knowers of truth had not undertaken out of fear of the vast expenditure of meaning, was elevated to high renown in the world.

children.text: kavīnāṃ kiṃ dattair nṛpapaśubhir anyair avasare paraṃ pṛthvīpālaḥ kṣaṇam api sa karṇo vitaratu /
anāttaṃ tattvajñair api suvipulārthavyayabhiyā pratiṣṭhāṃ yena uccair jagati gamitaṃ rāmacaritam //
NB \msC\ reads here (instead of this verse?)
pālānvayāmbujavanaikavirocanāya tasmai namo 'stu yuvarājanareśvarāya /
children.translated_text: To that sovereign prince of men, the sole sun for the lotus-garden of the <s>Pāla</s> dynasty, I bow;

children.text: koṭipradānaghaṭitojjvalakīrtimūrtir yenāmaratvapadavīṃ gamito 'bhinandaḥ //
children.translated_text: By whom <s>Abhinanda</s> was granted the path of immortality, his form of fame made brilliant through gifts of ten million.

children.text: pālānvayāmbujavanaikavirocanāya tasmai namo 'stu yuvarājanareśvarāya /
koṭipradānaghaṭitojjvalakīrtimūrtir yena amaratvapadavīṃ gamito 'bhinandaḥ //
tṛtīyaḥ sargaḥ
children.translated_text: Third Canto

children.text: atha prabuddhaḥ prathamaṃ vibuddham āsīnam ādāya tadaṅghriyugmam /
children.translated_text: Then [<s>Rāma</s>], having awakened first, taking hold of the feet of the one who was already awake and seated [<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>] —

children.text: prakāmanidrābhigamābhirāmo rāmaḥ sumitrāsutam ity uvāca //
children.translated_text: charming from the pleasure of deep sleep — <s>Rāma</s> spoke thus to the son of <s>Sumitrā</s>:

children.text: atha prabuddhaḥ prathamaṃ vibuddham āsīnam ādāya tadaṅghriyugmam /
prakāmanidrābhigamābhirāmo rāmaḥ sumitrāsutam ity uvāca //
kim ittham eva kṣapito niśīthaḥ kaccin muhūrārdham asi prasuptaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Was the midnight spent just like this? Have you slept even half a <s>muhūrta</s> (a short while)?

children.text: asmin prasādāvasare dhiyāṃ ca pratiṣṭhitaś cetasi kas tavārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: In this auspicious time of mental clarity, what purpose is settled in your mind?

children.text: kim ittham eva kṣapito niśīthaḥ kaccin muhūrārdham asi prasuptaḥ /
asmin prasādāvasare dhiyāṃ ca pratiṣṭhitaś cetasi kas tava arthaḥ //
vanaukasas tasya naveśvarasya bhāvāvabodhāya punar vimṛśya /
children.translated_text: "To ascertain the disposition of that new lord of the forest-dwellers [<s>Sugrīva</s>], after further deliberation,

children.text: yat prāptakālaṃ tad udāharāśu prasthānakālo 'yam atipraśastaḥ //
children.translated_text: State quickly what is timely — this hour of departure is most auspicious.

children.text: vanaukasas tasya naveśvarasya bhāvāvabodhāya punar vimṛśya /
yat prāptakālaṃ tad udāharā aśu prasthānakālo 'yam atipraśastaḥ //
svakāryalābhastimitaḥ kapiś cen na kaścid artho 'nusṛtena tena /
children.translated_text: "If the monkey is motionless, absorbed in gaining his own ends, then there is no purpose in pursuing him.

children.text: ripaūpetaṃ varam arthibhāvād vikārasaṃdehasahe na mitre //
children.translated_text: better an enemy approached out of supplication than a friend who cannot withstand the suspicion of change.

children.text: svakāryalābhastimitaḥ kapiś cen na kaścid artho 'nusṛtena tena /
ripau upetaṃ varam arthibhāvād vikārasaṃdehasahe na mitre //
kāryāntarāśārahitena tena vyaktaṃ khalenādya vayaṃ nirastāḥ /
children.translated_text: We have clearly been rejected today by that ungrateful wretch, devoid of concern for other tasks;

children.text: dattaḥ pradīrghāgrahaṇābhidhāno yenāyam ārād api no 'rdhacandraḥ //
children.translated_text: he has given us this half-moon [gesture of dismissal], which goes by the name of 'extended non-seizure,' even from afar.

children.text: kāryāntarāśārahitena tena vyaktaṃ khalena adya vayaṃ nirastāḥ /
dattaḥ pradīrghāgrahaṇābhidhāno yena ayam ārād api no 'rdhacandraḥ //
ruddhas tapasvī sa kathaṃ na kaiścin mohāndhakūpe nipatan madāndhaḥ /
children.translated_text: How was that ascetic not restrained by anyone, falling blind with arrogance into the well of delusion?

children.text: kiṃ deśakās te 'pi hanūmadādyāḥ sadyaḥ padaṃ prāpya samaṃ vipannāḥ //
children.translated_text: Have those regional chiefs too — <s>Hanumān</s> and the rest — perished, having instantly attained the same fate?

children.text: ruddhas tapasvī sa kathaṃ na kaiścin mohāndhakūpe nipatan madāndhaḥ /
kiṃ deśakās te 'pi hanūmadādyāḥ sadyaḥ padaṃ prāpya samaṃ vipannāḥ //
riṣṭaṃ na dṛṣṭaṃ pavamānasūnor na cāgnisūnor na ca vālisūnoḥ /
children.translated_text: No calamity has been seen befalling the son of the Wind, nor the son of Fire, nor the son of <s>Vālin</s>;

children.text: sarve 'pi kiṃkāraṇam ekadaiva pramītakalpāḥ kapidārakās te //
children.translated_text: why then have all those monkey princes at once become as if slain?

children.text: riṣṭaṃ na dṛṣṭaṃ pavamānasūnor na ca agnisūnor na ca vālisūnoḥ /
sarve 'pi kiṃkāraṇam ekada aiva pramītakalpāḥ kapidārakās te //
sa durnivāro harir adya śetām āsvāditaiśvaryamadhur madena /
children.translated_text: That irresistible <s>Hari</s> (monkey-lord) now sleeps, intoxicated with the sweet liquor of tasted sovereignty;

children.text: kathaṃ punar jāgarakāla eva suptās tadāptā iti me vitarkaḥ //
children.translated_text: but how is it that his trusted companions too are asleep, even though it is the waking hour? — this is my doubt.

children.text: sa durnivāro harir adya śetām āsvāditaiśvaryamadhur madena /
kathaṃ punar jāgarakāla eva suptās tadāptā iti me vitarkaḥ //
devāt prasūtena himetarāṃśor ūrjasvalais taiḥ sakhibhir vṛtena /
children.translated_text: By him, born of the god whose rays are unlike snow (i.e., the Sun), accompanied by those vigorous friends,

children.text: udāradehadyutināsmadarthe niranvayaṃ tena tamaḥ prapannam //
children.translated_text: whose bodily splendor was magnificent — by him, for our sake, darkness has been utterly vanquished.

children.text: devāt prasūtena himetarāṃśor ūrjasvalais taiḥ sakhibhir vṛtena /
udāradehadyutina āsmadarthe niranvayaṃ tena tamaḥ prapannam //
aho mahan mohajam andhakāraṃ yenādya madhyesabham uddhureṇa /
children.translated_text: Alas, great is this darkness born of delusion, by which that insolent one, in the midst of the assembly,

children.text: utsārya tān mantrimaṇipradīpān plavaṅgarājaḥ prasabhaṃ gṛhītaḥ //
children.translated_text: having thrust aside those lamp-like jewels of ministers, has forcibly seized the monkey-king.

children.text: aho mahan mohajam andhakāraṃ yena adya madhyesabham uddhureṇa /
utsārya tān mantrimaṇipradīpān plavaṅgarājaḥ prasabhaṃ gṛhītaḥ //
lobhasya mohasya manobhavasya madasya cātiprasaro na ruddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: The excess of greed, delusion, passion, and pride has not been restrained;

children.text: ruddhaḥ paraṃ pūrṇamanorathena tenādya naḥ pratyupakāravegaḥ //
children.translated_text: rather, by him whose desires are fully satisfied, the force of our repayment has now been blocked.

children.text: lobhasya mohasya manobhavasya madasya ca atiprasaro na ruddhaḥ /
ruddhaḥ paraṃ pūrṇamanorathena tena adya naḥ pratyupakāravegaḥ //
samrāṭpadasthasya padād apetāḥ samprītaye samprati mā sma bhūmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having fallen from the position of one established on the imperial throne, let us not now exist for his pleasure;

children.text: dṛṣṭāstrasārā api tasya bhīroḥ kiṃ bhītaye vatsa vayaṃ na bhūtāḥ //
children.translated_text: though we have witnessed the essence of his weapons, child, have we not become a source of fear for that coward?

children.text: samrāṭpadasthasya padād apetāḥ samprītaye samprati mā sma bhūmaḥ /
dṛṣṭāstrasārā api tasya bhīroḥ kiṃ bhītaye vatsa vayaṃ na bhūtāḥ //
sthāne nirastaḥ sudhiyāgrajena sa tena māyāmasṛṇo durātmā /
children.translated_text: Rightly was that wicked one, smooth with deception, rejected by our wise elder brother;

children.text: mayā madāndhena punar vṛthaiva kroṣṭā mṛgendrasya pade 'bhiṣiktaḥ //
children.translated_text: but by me, blinded by pride, a jackal was uselessly installed in the seat of a lion.

children.text: sthāne nirastaḥ sudhiya āgrajena sa tena māyāmasṛṇo durātmā /
mayā madāndhena punar vṛtha aiva kroṣṭā mṛgendrasya pade 'bhiṣiktaḥ //
nirveśaniryātanaśāṭhyanidrāṃ nīceṣu daṇḍaḥ paruṣo nihanti /
children.translated_text: Harsh punishment destroys in the base their sleep of indolence, ingratitude, and deceit;

children.text: tathāpi dākṣiṇyavilambitavyam idaṃ dhanus taṃ prati māmakīnam //
children.translated_text: yet, this bow of mine must be delayed by courtesy toward him.

children.text: nirveśaniryātanaśāṭhyanidrāṃ nīceṣu daṇḍaḥ paruṣo nihanti /
tatha āpi dākṣiṇyavilambitavyam idaṃ dhanus taṃ prati māmakīnam //
yāvan na viśrāmyati vegajanmā dikṣu dhvanir vālibhidaḥ śarasya /
children.translated_text: So long as the echo born of the speed of the arrow of <s>Vālin</s>'s slayer does not cease in the directions,

children.text: tāvat punas taṅka iha trilokyām ākrāntakiṣkindham upakrameta //
children.translated_text: until then, let no invader in the three worlds attempt [to attack] this place that has conquered <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>.

children.text: yāvan na viśrāmyati vegajanmā dikṣu dhvanir vālibhidaḥ śarasya /
tāvat punas taṅka iha trilokyām ākrāntakiṣkindham upakrameta //
asmāsu nāvedayati sma garvāt kurvīta śeṣārivadhaṃ bhujābhyām /
children.translated_text: Out of pride he does not inform us; he would accomplish the slaying of the remaining enemies with his own arms;

children.text: vidhāya saurājyam asaūpeyād ity arthitā paśyati na pramāṇam //
children.translated_text: having established good governance, he would come [to us] — thus do the petitioned [ministers] advise, but he sees no authority [in their words].

children.text: asmāsu nā avedayati sma garvāt kurvīta śeṣārivadhaṃ bhujābhyām /
vidhāya saurājyam asau upeyād ity arthitā paśyati na pramāṇam //
tad eṣa me nirmalasargasargaḥ ṣaḍvargaruddho ripuvat sa heyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this [brother] of mine, born of a pure lineage, restrained by the six [enemies], is to be abandoned like a foe;

children.text: nāsau niṣiddhas tava yānapakṣo mayā bata prāg asamāhitena //
children.translated_text: and this plan of yours to depart was not forbidden by me earlier, when I was distracted. Alas!

children.text: tad eṣa me nirmalasargasargaḥ ṣaḍvargaruddho ripuvat sa heyaḥ /
na asau niṣiddhas tava yānapakṣo mayā bata prāg asamāhitena //
asaṃśayaṃ sa pratihārapālīsasambhramāveditasannikarṣam /
children.translated_text: Without doubt, when he learns of your approach, announced by the agitation of the door-keepers,

children.text: tvāṃ praty asūyāṃ hṛdayena dhāsyaty upasthitāntaḥpuraviprayogaḥ //
children.translated_text: he will harbor jealousy in his heart toward you, being faced with separation from the inner chambers.

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ sa pratihārapālīsasambhramāveditasannikarṣam /
tvāṃ praty asūyāṃ hṛdayena dhāsyaty upasthitāntaḥpuraviprayogaḥ //
tadvaktram ārkes taruṇārkatāmraṃ tvatprītivākyair akṛtapramodam /
children.translated_text: That face of his, coppery as the young sun, not yet gladdened by your affectionate words,

children.text: bhaviṣyati pratyupakārabhāranirvāhacintāgamasāndhakāram //
children.translated_text: will become darkened with anxious thought about how to bear the burden of repayment.

children.text: tadvaktram ārkes taruṇārkatāmraṃ tvatprītivākyair akṛtapramodam /
bhaviṣyati pratyupakārabhāranirvāhacintāgamasāndhakāram //
smariṣyati tvāṃ na sa bodhyamāno 'py ālokayiṣyaty athavā na pṛṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: He will not remember you even when reminded, or else, if asked, he will not look [at you];

children.text: pratyeṣi kāntājanamadhyavartī sa cintayāsmadgatayādhunāste //
children.translated_text: you will return, lingering amidst your beloved's attendants, while he sits now brooding with thoughts about our affairs.

children.text: smariṣyati tvāṃ na sa bodhyamāno 'py ālokayiṣyaty athavā na pṛṣṭaḥ /
pratyeṣi kāntājanamadhyavartī sa cintaya āsmadgataya ādhunā āste //
āvāṃ yadaivādritaṭe niviṣṭau sa kālikāṃ vīkṣya purīṃ praviṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: The very moment when we two were seated on the mountain slope and he, having seen <s>Kālikā</s>, entered the city —

children.text: āmṛṣṭam āsīc capalena tena sauhārdam asmadviṣayaṃ tadaiva //
children.translated_text: at that very moment the friendship that he bore toward us was wiped away by that fickle one.

children.text: āvāṃ yada aiva adritaṭe niviṣṭau sa kālikāṃ vīkṣya purīṃ praviṣṭaḥ /
āmṛṣṭam āsīc capalena tena sauhārdam asmadviṣayaṃ tada aiva //
ahaḥsv amīṣu kṣaṇa eva nāsīd āsīn na saṃdeśaharo 'nurūpaḥ /
children.translated_text: In these days there was not even a moment [of leisure]; there was no suitable messenger;

children.text: ityādi sa vyaktam alīkam eva tvatprītyupālambhapadeṣu vaktā //
children.translated_text: such and similar things he will clearly speak — all falsehoods — as pretexts for reproaching your affection.

children.text: ahaḥsv amīṣu kṣaṇa eva nā asīd āsīn na saṃdeśaharo 'nurūpaḥ /
ityādi sa vyaktam alīkam eva tvatprītyupālambhapadeṣu vaktā //
kṛtāvahelaḥ praṇayaprasannaṃ niruttaraḥ satvarakāryavādam /
children.translated_text: Having shown contempt, rendered speechless before your gracious, affectionate, and urgent demand for action,

children.text: prekṣiṣyate roṣalavānuraktaṃ valīmukhaḥ śuṣkamukho mukhaṃ te //
children.translated_text: he, <s>Vālīmukha</s> (Sugrīva), dry-faced, will gaze at your face, tinged with a trace of anger.

children.text: kṛtāvahelaḥ praṇayaprasannaṃ niruttaraḥ satvarakāryavādam /
prekṣiṣyate roṣalavānuraktaṃ valīmukhaḥ śuṣkamukho mukhaṃ te //
tasyāgamād yaḥ sahasā bhaviṣyaty arthasya tasyābhavanaṃ mamāstu /
children.translated_text: Let me not possess the purpose that will suddenly arise from his arrival;

children.text: bādhiṣyate vālivadhātiriktas tadveśmayātrānuśayaḥ sadā nau //
children.translated_text: the regret of that visit to his dwelling, exceeding even the slaying of <s>Vālin</s>, will always torment us both.

children.text: tasyā agamād yaḥ sahasā bhaviṣyaty arthasya tasya abhavanaṃ mama astu /
bādhiṣyate vālivadhātiriktas tadveśmayātrānuśayaḥ sadā nau //
sa prāktano nūnam anarthabhājā nītas talaṃ tena hitaiṣivargaḥ /
children.translated_text: Surely that former circle of well-wishers has been brought low by that one destined for misfortune;

children.text: utthāpitair dūram asāv idānīṃ divāniśaṃ dīvyati durvidagdhaiḥ //
children.translated_text: having raised up deceitful ones from afar, he now gambles day and night with those ill-counseled fools.

children.text: sa prāktano nūnam anarthabhājā nītas talaṃ tena hitaiṣivargaḥ /
utthāpitair dūram asāv idānīṃ divāniśaṃ dīvyati durvidagdhaiḥ //
akṣā mṛgākṣyo mṛgayā madhūni prekṣāś ca tasyādya haranti kālam /
children.translated_text: Dice, doe-eyed women, hunting, wines, and spectacles now consume his time;

children.text: na prāpnuvanti kṣaṇam āptavācaḥ sadādṛtāś cāraṇacāṭuvādāḥ //
children.translated_text: the words of trusted [advisors] do not reach him for a moment, while the flattering speeches of bards are always honored.

children.text: akṣā mṛgākṣyo mṛgayā madhūni prekṣāś ca tasya adya haranti kālam /
na prāpnuvanti kṣaṇam āptavācaḥ sadādṛtāś cāraṇacāṭuvādāḥ //
vadanti bhītāḥ sacivā na kiṃcit kiṃ cintayāsmadgatayā viṭānām /
children.translated_text: The frightened ministers say nothing; what concern have buffoons with thoughts about our affairs?

children.text: svayaṃ na sampraty anusaṃdadhāti pūrvāparaṃ kāmaparaḥ sa rājā //
children.translated_text: That king, devoted to pleasure, does not himself now deliberate on what comes before and after.

children.text: vadanti bhītāḥ sacivā na kiṃcit kiṃ cintaya āsmadgatayā viṭānām /
svayaṃ na sampraty anusaṃdadhāti pūrvāparaṃ kāmaparaḥ sa rājā //
na sūrayo na sthavirā na dhīrāḥ puraḥsthitāḥ prāśnikatāṃ prayānti /
children.translated_text: Neither scholars, nor elders, nor the steadfast stand before him to serve as counselors;

children.text: saṃtiṣṭhate saṃsadi saṃśayānaḥ pṛṣṭhopaviṣṭāsu vilāsinīṣu //
children.translated_text: he sits in the assembly, wavering, while courtesans are seated behind him.

children.text: na sūrayo na sthavirā na dhīrāḥ puraḥsthitāḥ prāśnikatāṃ prayānti /
saṃtiṣṭhate saṃsadi saṃśayānaḥ pṛṣṭhopaviṣṭāsu vilāsinīṣu //
itthaṃgate tatra gatasya kena manyus tavodīrṇarayo nivāryaḥ /
children.translated_text: Under such circumstances, when you go there, by whom shall your anger, surging in its flow, be restrained?

children.text: vicāyamāṇo na guṇāya naḥ syād asau kapīnāṃ kadanānubandhaḥ //
children.translated_text: The ensuing slaughter of monkeys, if examined, would not be to our advantage.

children.text: itthaṃgate tatra gatasya kena manyus tava udīrṇarayo nivāryaḥ /
vicāyamāṇo na guṇāya naḥ syād asau kapīnāṃ kadanānubandhaḥ //
prapannaśāṭhyasya haṭhopanāmād āneṣyamāṇasya guṇaṃ na vīkṣe /
children.translated_text: I see no merit in one who has resorted to treachery, to be brought back by forceful summons;

children.text: tathāvidhā hi dviṣatāṃ stavena kaṣanti karṇau param antikasthāḥ //
children.translated_text: for such ones, when praised by enemies, merely scratch their ears while standing nearby.

children.text: prapannaśāṭhyasya haṭhopanāmād āneṣyamāṇasya guṇaṃ na vīkṣe /
tathāvidhā hi dviṣatāṃ stavena kaṣanti karṇau param antikasthāḥ //
spṛṣ.o na ced vikriyayā kayāpi nopasthitaḥ kāryavaśād idānīm /
children.translated_text: If he has not been touched by any transformation [of heart], and does not now present himself under compulsion of duty,

children.text: etu svayaṃ na kriyate vṛthaiva sa tvadbalātkāraniruddhaśobhaḥ //
children.translated_text: let him come of his own accord — let him not be made, needlessly, one whose splendor is suppressed by your coercion.

children.text: spṛṣ.o na ced vikriyayā kaya āpi na upasthitaḥ kāryavaśād idānīm /
etu svayaṃ na kriyate vṛtha aiva sa tvadbalātkāraniruddhaśobhaḥ //
yathāvayos tātajaṭāyuṣoktam uktaṃ kabandhena yathā ca tena /
children.translated_text: Just as was said to us by our father-like <s>Jaṭāyu</s>, and just as was said by <s>Kabandha</s>,

children.text: tathopayāsyaty acirād avaśyam āhūtacakro haricakravartī //
children.translated_text: so too the monkey-emperor, wielder of the discus, will surely come before long, summoned by destiny.

children.text: yathā āvayos tātajaṭāyuṣa ūktam uktaṃ kabandhena yathā ca tena /
tatha ūpayāsyaty acirād avaśyam āhūtacakro haricakravartī //
yat satyam ādityasamudbhavatvād udbhūtim eṣyanti guṇās tadīyāḥ /
children.translated_text: In truth, since he is born of the Sun, his virtues will inevitably manifest;

children.text: tulāgrasampātavilambadoṣe tasmin visaṃvādam ahaṃ na śaṅke //
children.translated_text: in him, who has the fault of delay like the tilting of a balance's beam, I do not suspect any breach of faith.

children.text: yat satyam ādityasamudbhavatvād udbhūtim eṣyanti guṇās tadīyāḥ /
tulāgrasampātavilambadoṣe tasmin visaṃvādam ahaṃ na śaṅke //
viropataptasya videśavāsād ājagmuṣas tasya nijādhivāsam /
children.translated_text: For him, scorched by the enemy's heat and dwelling abroad, now returning to his own abode,

children.text: iyanty ahāny utsukabandhuvargasaṃvargaṇavyagratayaiva yānti //
children.translated_text: these few days will pass in the preoccupation of reuniting with his eager group of kinsmen.

children.text: viropataptasya videśavāsād ājagmuṣas tasya nijādhivāsam /
iyanty ahāny utsukabandhuvargasaṃvargaṇavyagrataya aiva yānti //
sa nūnam āyāsyati vānarendraḥ saṃdeśakārpaṇyam asaṃmataṃ me /
children.translated_text: That lord of monkeys will surely come — sending a message is, in my opinion, ignoble;

children.text: sarvasvabhūtaṃ visṛjanti vatsa kāryātipāte 'pi na dhairyam āryāḥ //
children.translated_text: the noble ones give up everything that is their own, O child, but they do not abandon steadfastness even when a task is overdue.

children.text: sa nūnam āyāsyati vānarendraḥ saṃdeśakārpaṇyam asaṃmataṃ me /
sarvasvabhūtaṃ visṛjanti vatsa kāryātipāte 'pi na dhairyam āryāḥ //
vyatītavighnaḥ suhṛdarthanighno na śītalaḥ sthāsyati kiṃ gatena /
children.translated_text: Having overcome obstacles, destroying the enemy's purpose — will he remain cold? What is gained by going [there]?

children.text: sa tvaryamāṇas tvaramāṇa eva dhairyasya naḥ pāram avāpsyatīva //
children.translated_text: He, though urged, himself hastening, will soon reach the limit of our patience, as it were.

children.text: vyatītavighnaḥ suhṛdarthanighno na śītalaḥ sthāsyati kiṃ gatena /
sa tvaryamāṇas tvaramāṇa eva dhairyasya naḥ pāram avāpsyati iva //
dhig astu māṃ taṃ prati vipratīpam āśaṅkitaṃ tad bahu yena yad vā /
children.translated_text: Shame on me for harboring suspicion toward him — whatever much or little [suspicion] there was;

children.text: svakāryadolāsu jano 'lpabhāgyaḥ prāṅ niścinoti vyatirekam eva //
children.translated_text: a person of meager fortune, on the swings of his own affairs, first determines only the worst outcome.

children.text: dhig astu māṃ taṃ prati vipratīpam āśaṅkitaṃ tad bahu yena yad vā /
svakāryadolāsu jano 'lpabhāgyaḥ prāṅ niścinoti vyatirekam eva //
itthaṃ na māṃ pratyupapattim eti tatrādyapakṣadvitaye 'pi yātrā /
children.translated_text: Thus, a journey there does not commend itself to me — neither the first nor the second alternative;

children.text: varaṃ visoḍhāni kiyanty apīha saṅkhyātakālābhyadhikāny ahāni //
children.translated_text: better to have endured here, even for many days, in numbers exceeding the counted time.

children.text: itthaṃ na māṃ pratyupapattim eti tatrā adyapakṣadvitaye 'pi yātrā /
varaṃ visoḍhāni kiyanty api iha saṅkhyātakālābhyadhikāny ahāni //
svālocitaṃ vaktu bhavān idānīm ity anuṣṭheyam asaṃśayaṃ yat /
children.translated_text: Now let Your Honor speak your own considered view — what is to be carried out without doubt;

children.text: bālyāt prabhṛty eva tavottarā dhīr na pūrvapakṣe 'bhiniveśam eti //
children.translated_text: from childhood itself your later judgment [has always prevailed], never clinging to the first proposition.

children.text: svālocitaṃ vaktu bhavān idānīm ity anuṣṭheyam asaṃśayaṃ yat /
bālyāt prabhṛty eva tava uttarā dhīr na pūrvapakṣe 'bhiniveśam eti //
iti prasannāṃ giram agrajasya śrutvā cirād vītaviṣādapaṅkaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard the gracious speech of his elder brother, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the son of <s>Sumitrā</s>, long freed from the mire of despondency,

children.text: mukhaśriyaivojjvalayābhinandann idaṃ sumitrātanayo jagāda //
children.translated_text: as if illuminating [the scene] with the beauty of his face, spoke with approval thus:

children.text: iti prasannāṃ giram agrajasya śrutvā cirād vītaviṣādapaṅkaḥ /
mukhaśriya aiva ujjvalaya ābhinandann idaṃ sumitrātanayo jagāda //
samarthitaṃ sādhu samastam eva kṛtī kapiḥ kiṃ bahunoditena /
children.translated_text: 'Everything has been well justified. The capable monkey — what more need be said?

children.text: pravyaktam apy etad adoṣadṛṣṭyā gṛhītam āryeṇa na yat tadāgaḥ //
children.translated_text: Even what was manifest has been taken by Your Honor with a faultless eye — that was not his offense.

children.text: samarthitaṃ sādhu samastam eva kṛtī kapiḥ kiṃ bahuna ūditena /
pravyaktam apy etad adoṣadṛṣṭyā gṛhītam āryeṇa na yat tadāgaḥ //
tasyorjitenātiraver avadyaṃ naivekṣate 'ntaḥkaraṇaṃ mamāpi /
children.translated_text: His inner heart, enriched with vigorous power, does not perceive any fault either in my view;

children.text: ayaṃ punas tena kuto na jānāmy atikramaḥ kālakṛto na dṛṣṭaḥ //
children.translated_text: but this transgression [committed] by him — I do not know whence it comes — has not been seen as caused by time.

children.text: tasyā urjitena atiraver avadyaṃ na evā ikṣate 'ntaḥkaraṇaṃ mama api /
ayaṃ punas tena kuto na jānāmy atikramaḥ kālakṛto na dṛṣṭaḥ //
visarjitā vā punarāgamāya samāpatanty adya na te nalādyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Perhaps those [messengers] like <s>Nala</s> and others, dispatched to return [with information], have not yet arrived today;

children.text: samāharatiudyatavittavarṣo varṣāntarebhyaḥ pravarān harīn vā //
children.translated_text: or perhaps he is gathering, with readied showers of wealth, the finest monkeys from beyond the rainy seasons.

children.text: visarjitā vā punarāgamāya samāpatanty adya na te nalādyāḥ /
samāharatiudyatavittavarṣo varṣāntarebhyaḥ pravarān harīn vā //
aṣṭādaśadvīpakapīndramaulir maulān asau vālivadhapralīnān /
children.translated_text: That one, crowned jewel among the monkey-chiefs of the eighteen continents, [is gathering] the principal ones who had hidden after <s>Vālin</s>'s death,

children.text: naikābhyupāyopahitān idānīm uta pratīcchaty atisatkriyābhiḥ //
children.translated_text: and those now won over through manifold stratagems — he receives them with supreme honors.

children.text: aṣṭādaśadvīpakapīndramaulir maulān asau vālivadhapralīnān /
naikābhyupāyopahitān idānīm uta pratīcchaty atisatkriyābhiḥ //
aprāptasaṃtoṣam asaṃvibhaktasambhuktasarvasvam anuplaveṣu /
children.translated_text: Having not yet attained satisfaction, having shared and enjoyed his entire wealth among the refugees,

children.text: athādiśaty arpitasārakośaḥ prakāmapātheyaparigrahāya //
children.translated_text: and now, having committed his essential treasury, he directs them to provision themselves abundantly for the journey.

children.text: aprāptasaṃtoṣam asaṃvibhaktasambhuktasarvasvam anuplaveṣu /
athā adiśaty arpitasārakośaḥ prakāmapātheyaparigrahāya //
atho sa bhītāturabālavṛddhān vṛddhopasevī sanibhaṃ niyuṅkte /
children.translated_text: Or else he, who reveres elders, assigns <s>Nibha</s> (his son) together with the frightened, distressed, young, and old,

children.text: yathāyathaṃ sadmani padmasaṃkhyāsametaśākhāmṛgayūthanāthaḥ //
children.translated_text: as lord of monkey-troops arranged in companies numbered by lotus and conch [formations], each in their proper dwelling.

children.text: atho sa bhītāturabālavṛddhān vṛddhopasevī sanibhaṃ niyuṅkte /
yathāyathaṃ sadmani padmasaṃkhyāsametaśākhāmṛgayūthanāthaḥ //
tad ittham utthānasamākulatvān na tvaryamāṇo 'pi sa dūṣaṇāya /
children.translated_text: Therefore, since he is so engrossed in preparations, even though urged, he is not to be blamed;

children.text: āryeṇa tatrāpy asamāgatasya chāyācyutiḥ kaiva nirūpitā me //
children.translated_text: and for one who has not yet arrived — even there — what loss of allegiance has been determined regarding me, by Your Honor?

children.text: tad ittham utthānasamākulatvān na tvaryamāṇo 'pi sa dūṣaṇāya /
āryeṇa tatra apy asamāgatasya chāyācyutiḥ ka aiva nirūpitā me //
jñeyo 'sti naḥ pūrvam arer udantas tatas tadantāya vidheyam asti /
children.translated_text: First, the situation of the enemy must be known to us; then what is to be done for its resolution must be determined;

children.text: ity ākulatvān mama tāvad ārya kāryopataptiḥ kṣamate na dhairyam //
children.translated_text: therefore, O noble one, for now, my anxiety about our task does not permit patience.

children.text: jñeyo 'sti naḥ pūrvam arer udantas tatas tadantāya vidheyam asti /
ity ākulatvān mama tāvad ārya kāryopataptiḥ kṣamate na dhairyam //
anarthibhāvād upacāravādād ākāragupteś ca parībhavanti /
children.translated_text: By lack of supplication, by ceremonious words, and by concealment of one's true feelings, [people] offend [friends];

children.text: yathātathārthapratipādanena prayānti mitrāṇi nirantaratvam //
children.translated_text: through forthright communication of things as they truly are, friends attain unbroken closeness.

children.text: anarthibhāvād upacāravādād ākāragupteś ca parībhavanti /
yathātathārthapratipādanena prayānti mitrāṇi nirantaratvam //
mithaḥ prasādaskhalanād upādher upaiti sakhyaṃ khalayoḥ khilatvam /
children.translated_text: Between two wicked persons, through mutual lapses in goodwill arising from some cause, friendship becomes barren;

children.text: gṛhṇāti satpūruṣayor na doṣam audāryasaṃvādakṛtā tu maitrī //
children.translated_text: but a friendship formed by the accord of generosity between two noble persons does not seize upon faults.

children.text: mithaḥ prasādaskhalanād upādher upaiti sakhyaṃ khalayoḥ khilatvam /
gṛhṇāti satpūruṣayor na doṣam audāryasaṃvādakṛtā tu maitrī //
niryantraṇaṃ yatra na vartitavyaṃ na moditavyaṃ praṇayātivāde /
children.translated_text: Where one should not act without restraint, where one should not rejoice at an excess of affection,

children.text: viśaṅkitānyonyabhayaṃ vidūrān namaskriyām arhati sauhṛdaṃ tat //
children.translated_text: where there is mutual fear born of suspicion from afar — such a friendship deserves only a formal salutation.

children.text: niryantraṇaṃ yatra na vartitavyaṃ na moditavyaṃ praṇayātivāde /
viśaṅkitānyonyabhayaṃ vidūrān namaskriyām arhati sauhṛdaṃ tat //
visrabdham ājñāpaya kiṃ karomi kathaṃ ghaṭena plavagādhirājaḥ /
children.translated_text: Command me confidently — what shall I do? How shall the lord of monkeys be brought to act?

children.text: yat kiṃcid ādiśya nibhena kiṃ māṃ niṣedhasi kleśam ivekṣamāṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: Having assigned some task, why do you restrain me through <s>Nibha</s>, as if regarding it as an affliction?

children.text: visrabdham ājñāpaya kiṃ karomi kathaṃ ghaṭena plavagādhirājaḥ /
yat kiṃcid ādiśya nibhena kiṃ māṃ niṣedhasi kleśam ivā ikṣamāṇaḥ //
sthito 'smi tāvad dinam etad eṣyaty anyedyur ājñāṃ tava na pratīkṣe /
children.translated_text: I shall remain for this day — he will come tomorrow; I do not await your command;

children.text: āryo 'nurodhān na yunakti yatra tatrāham ambāniyamāt svatantraḥ //
children.translated_text: where Your Honor, out of consideration, does not assign a task, there I am free by mother's ordinance.

children.text: sthito 'smi tāvad dinam etad eṣyaty anyedyur ājñāṃ tava na pratīkṣe /
āryo 'nurodhān na yunakti yatra tatra aham ambāniyamāt svatantraḥ //
tad eṣa niṣkramya tathā karomi tatpūrvasaṅgaḥ plavago yathāśu /
children.translated_text: So, going forth, I shall act in such a way that that monkey, with his former bond, may swiftly

children.text: taṃ vairisaṃhāramahopakāram āryāya niryātayituṃ yatena //
children.translated_text: be made to deliver to Your Honor that great service of destroying the enemy.

children.text: tad eṣa niṣkramya tathā karomi tatpūrvasaṅgaḥ plavago yathā āśu /
taṃ vairisaṃhāramahopakāram āryāya niryātayituṃ yatena //
dhik taṃ dhanuṣpāṇim anuplavaṃ māṃ mudhā manaḥparyuṣitāvalepam /
children.translated_text: Shame on me, a monkey-less bowman, vainly stale in my pride of mind,

children.text: anvīkṣate yasya mamāvasādād āryaḥ sahāyāntaram antarajñaḥ //
children.translated_text: whose decline Your Honor, the discerner of inner [qualities], watches while looking toward another ally.

children.text: dhik taṃ dhanuṣpāṇim anuplavaṃ māṃ mudhā manaḥparyuṣitāvalepam /
anvīkṣate yasya mama avasādād āryaḥ sahāyāntaram antarajñaḥ //
dhikśātatāṃ sannataparvatāṃ dhig dhik pātavegaṃ ca mamāśugānām /
children.translated_text: Shame on the bowstring's tautness, shame on the mountains it has bent, shame on the speed of flight of my arrows,

children.text: alakṣitoddeśam api dviṣantaṃ nihatya nāyānti hi yat kṣaṇena //
children.translated_text: which do not, in an instant, slay the enemy, even one whose whereabouts are unknown!

children.text: dhikśātatāṃ sannataparvatāṃ dhig dhik pātavegaṃ ca mamā aśugānām /
alakṣitoddeśam api dviṣantaṃ nihatya nā ayānti hi yat kṣaṇena //
kharādirakṣaḥkadaneṣu dīrgham amī parijñātarasāḥ kim anyat /
children.translated_text: In the slaughter of <s>Rākṣasas</s> beginning with <s>Khara</s>, these [arrows], whose taste has long been known — what else [is needed]?

children.text: asṛgbhujāṃ bhoktum asṛk tvarantāṃ bhūyo 'pi bhūcandra tavārdhacandrāḥ //
children.translated_text: Your half-moon [arrows], O lord of the earth, are eager once more to drink the blood of those who feast on blood.

children.text: kharādirakṣaḥkadaneṣu dīrgham amī parijñātarasāḥ kim anyat /
asṛgbhujāṃ bhoktum asṛk tvarantāṃ bhūyo 'pi bhūcandra tava ardhacandrāḥ //
ātāṭakāsaṃjñapanāt prapannas tvayaiṣa varṇāśramarakṣaṇāya /
children.translated_text: Approached by you for the protection of <s>varṇa</s> (social order) and <s>āśrama</s> (stages of life) since the destruction of <s>Ātāṭaka</s> (<s>Tāṭakā</s>),

children.text: samāpyatāṃ śeṣanibarhaṇena kṣapācarāṇāṃ nidhanādhikāraḥ //
children.translated_text: let this charge of exterminating the night-wanderers be completed by annihilating the remainder.

children.text: ātāṭakāsaṃjñapanāt prapannas tvaya aiṣa varṇāśramarakṣaṇāya /
samāpyatāṃ śeṣanibarhaṇena kṣapācarāṇāṃ nidhanādhikāraḥ //
uddhṛtya ghorāyudhavṛndavṛṣṭim anuṣṭhitām oghaśaravyayena /
children.translated_text: Having lifted the terrible shower of a multitude of weapons, unleashed through a flood of arrows,

children.text: sa rākṣasebhyo 'mbaragocarebhyas trātas tvayaikena makho maharṣeḥ //
children.translated_text: the <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice) of the great sage was protected by you alone from the <s>Rākṣasas</s> who roam the sky.

children.text: uddhṛtya ghorāyudhavṛndavṛṣṭim anuṣṭhitām oghaśaravyayena /
sa rākṣasebhyo 'mbaragocarebhyas trātas tvaya aikena makho maharṣeḥ //
taṃ kālakalpaṃ kiyatā śrameṇa tathāvadhīr mārgarudhaṃ virādham /
children.translated_text: With how little effort did you slay <s>Virādha</s>, that death-like one blocking the path?

children.text: āsan muhūrtāḥ kati ca ghnatas te sainyaṃ janasthānapateḥ svarasya //
children.translated_text: And how many minutes did it take you to destroy the army of <s>Svara</s> (<s>Khara</s>), the lord of <s>Janasthāna</s>?

children.text: taṃ kālakalpaṃ kiyatā śrameṇa tatha āvadhīr mārgarudhaṃ virādham /
āsan muhūrtāḥ kati ca ghnatas te sainyaṃ janasthānapateḥ svarasya //
āsīt kṣuraprasya kiyān vilambaḥ krūreṣu teṣu triśiraḥśiraḥsu /
children.translated_text: How brief was the delay of the razor[-sharp arrow] upon those cruel three heads of <s>Triśiras</s>?

children.text: katīṣavo dūṣaṇadehayātrānivāraṇārthaṃ ca raṇe visṛṣṭāḥ //
children.translated_text: And how many arrows were discharged in battle to prevent the journey of <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>'s body [i.e., to slay him]?

children.text: āsīt kṣuraprasya kiyān vilambaḥ krūreṣu teṣu triśiraḥśiraḥsu /
kati iṣavo dūṣaṇadehayātrānivāraṇārthaṃ ca raṇe visṛṣṭāḥ //
kasyāvalambād akarot parāsuṃ mārīcam uccāvacamāyam āryaḥ /
children.translated_text: Upon whose support did Your Honor make <s>Mārīca</s>, master of manifold illusions, breathless?

children.translated_text: And by you alone was that lord of the night-wanderers too identified and humbled in the directions.

ity aprapañcoditakāraṇāni mithas tayos tathyaguṇagrahāṇi /
children.translated_text: Thus, [exchanging] sincere recognitions of each other's true virtues, with causes stated without elaboration,

children.translated_text: the birds in their nests, having reached a single accord, sang out as if offering praises.

children.text: ity aprapañcoditakāraṇāni mithas tayos tathyaguṇagrahāṇi /
neduḥ stuvānā iva sūnṛtāni khagāḥ kulāyeṣu kṛtaikamatyāḥ //
āropya sandhyāṃ diśi vajrapāṇeḥ paryasya candraṃ kakubhi pratīcyām /
children.translated_text: Having raised the twilight in the eastern direction of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> (<s>Indra</s>), and having turned the moon about in the western quarter,

children.text: utsaṅgitoḍuprakarā khagānām ādāya nidrāṃ rajanī jagāma //
children.translated_text: the night departed, taking with it sleep, having gathered up the host of stars into her lap, along with the birds.

children.text: āropya sandhyāṃ diśi vajrapāṇeḥ paryasya candraṃ kakubhi pratīcyām /

kaviś ca jīvaś ca sutaś ca bhūmeḥ sa dakṣiṇāśātilako muniś ca /
children.translated_text: The poet [Venus], and the living one [Mercury], and the son of the Earth [Mars], and that distinguished sage, the ornament of the southern direction [Canopus],

children.text: āsannasūryāṃśubhayadrutasya kṣaṇaṃ rarakṣur bhagaṇasya pṛṣṭham //
children.translated_text: for a moment guarded the rear of the starry host, fleeing in terror of the approaching rays of the sun.

children.text: kaviś ca jīvaś ca sutaś ca bhūmeḥ sa dakṣiṇāśātilako muniś ca /
āsannasūryāṃśubhayadrutasya kṣaṇaṃ rarakṣur bhagaṇasya pṛṣṭham //
dig darśayāmāsa mukhaṃ sarāgaṃ na yāvad aindrī gaṇikeva mattā /

children.translated_text: than the lord of birds [the moon] entered the lap of the ocean, fearing a spray of the red evening-[redness of dawn].

children.translated_text: The moon, having released its stars, lingered for a moment; nor was there yet darkness at the edges;

children.text: bhṛśaṃ diśīndrasya rarāja sandhyā sindūriṇīva graharājamudrā //
children.translated_text: the twilight of <s>Indra</s>'s direction blazed intensely, like the vermilion seal of the king of planets [the sun].

children.translated_text: As if plucking aloft the star-buds, spreading a most intense reddish glow,

children.translated_text: As if grasping a branch — the direction of <s>Maghon</s> (<s>Indra</s>) — the twilight climbed the sky-tree.

children.translated_text: The twilight, as if seized by an excess of passion for gathering the remaining clusters of star-blossoms,

children.text: apy uccakaiḥ pūrvamahīdhramūrdhni sthitvā viyadbhūruham āruroha //
children.translated_text: having first stood atop the peak of the eastern mountain, climbed the sky-tree even higher.

children.translated_text: bore the tender, young-lip-soft nets of twilight-colored blossom-clusters.

children.translated_text: the radiant twilight, like the colored dust of a theater-stage, spread across the arena of the sky.

children.translated_text: Cognitions bright with immersion in truth, as though worldly passion had ascended,

children.text: śanaiḥ śanair mlānaruco mamajjus tārāḥ prasarpaty aruṇe cireṇa //
children.translated_text: slowly, slowly lost their luster — the stars sank as the reddish dawn crept forward at length.

children.text: saṃvittayas tattvavigāhaśubhrāḥ sāṃsārike rāga iva adhirūḍhe /

kaiḥ śikṣitā vartayituṃ tadāsīd unmīlitaṃ tūlikayeva citram /
children.translated_text: By whom was that infant twilight taught to execute what seemed a painting

children.text: taraṅgavat tuṅgaśaradghanālīvisaṃsthule vyomani bālasandhyā //
children.translated_text: unveiled by a brush, upon the sky's broad canvas, uneven with tall rows of autumn clouds?

children.text: kaiḥ śikṣitā vartayituṃ tadā āsīd unmīlitaṃ tūlikaya īva citram /
taraṅgavat tuṅgaśaradghanālīvisaṃsthule vyomani bālasandhyā //

children.translated_text: Just applied to the horizon of the lord of gods, anointed with a garland of broken cloud-waves,

children.text: babhau visarpaty ayasīva tailaṃ nabhastale bālapataṅgatejaḥ //
children.translated_text: the radiance of the young sun shone on the surface of the sky like oil of linseed spreading forth.

children.translated_text: The sky, though the rays of the cool-rayed moon had been swept clear, still bore a reddish hue when the hot-rayed sun appeared;

children.text: bharaṃ pratīcchanti mahodayānāṃ pātrāṇi paryāyavaśaṃvadāni //
children.translated_text: vessels obedient to the turn of succession bear the burden of the greatly rising.

children.text: prasattinirvyūḍhasudhāmayūkhaṃ kham uṣṇaraśmāv api raktim ūhe /

tāpiñchakalpaḥ kakubhi pratīcyām ācchādayāmāsa mṛgo mṛgāṅkam /
children.translated_text: In the western quarter, the deer-marked moon was hidden by a darkness like dark <s>tāmāla</s> leaves,

children.text: dūrādhirūḍhaṃ janam āpadīva prakāśamāno 'tiśayād avarṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: like a person who has climbed to a great height being overwhelmed by calamity, exceedingly diminished in appearance.

children.text: tāpiñchakalpaḥ kakubhi pratīcyām ācchādayāmāsa mṛgo mṛgāṅkam /
dūrādhirūḍhaṃ janam āpadi iva prakāśamāno 'tiśayād avarṇaḥ //
pradīptasandhyāgni nadaddvijaughaṃ niraṃśukadhvastaparāṅmukhendu /
children.translated_text: With the fire of twilight blazing, the flocks of birds crying out, the moon stripped of rays and turning its face away,

children.text: viyadviluptoḍukulaṃ tadābhūc cakrāntarākrāntapuropameyam //
children.translated_text: the sky, despoiled of its star-garments, appeared like a city invaded by an enemy army.

children.text: pradīptasandhyāgni nadaddvijaughaṃ niraṃśukadhvastaparāṅmukhendu /
viyadviluptoḍukulaṃ tada ābhūc cakrāntarākrāntapuropameyam //
mithaḥ kṛtālokamahotsavānāṃ kṛtāravaḥ sārasadampatīnām /
children.translated_text: Having made cries to each other, the <s>sārasa</s> (crane) couples celebrated a festival of mutual gazing,

children.text: na bālabhānoḥ kiraṇād abhaiṣīn nadīṣu nīhāramayo 'ndhakāraḥ //
children.translated_text: unafraid of the rays of the young sun — the misty darkness lingering upon the rivers.

children.text: mithaḥ kṛtālokamahotsavānāṃ kṛtāravaḥ sārasadampatīnām /

children.translated_text: Flocks of birds, crossing and having crossed the frost-darkness, chirping upon the rivers,

children.text: raktāravindasya rajobhir ārdrair aktā raviṃ vāriṇi vīkṣamāṇā //
children.translated_text: gazed at the sun [reflected] in the water, anointed with the moist pollen of red lotuses.

children.text: tatāra saṃtīrya himāndhakāraṃ tatā rasantī saritaḥ khagālī /
raktāravindasya rajobhir ārdrair aktā raviṃ vāriṇi vīkṣamāṇā //
smaravyayaklāntavalatpulindīsarvāṅgasaṃvāhakalāvidagdhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Skilled in the art of massaging every limb of the <s>Pulinda</s> women exhausted from the exertions of love-play,

children.text: vilambya kośeṣu kuśeśayānāṃ sasāra kāsārataraṅgavātaḥ //
children.translated_text: the wind from the lake-waves lingered in the sheaths of the lotuses and then moved on.

children.text: smaravyayaklāntavalatpulindīsarvāṅgasaṃvāhakalāvidagdhaḥ /

children.translated_text: Having left behind the coldness of the sand on the riverbanks, the sages bathed in the warm rivers,

children.text: apām apūryanta ca nairjharīṇāṃ kuṭā girigrāmakuṭumbinībhiḥ //
children.translated_text: and the hollows of the mountain-torrents were filled by the women of mountain villages.

children.text: atītya śaityaṃ taṭavālukānāṃ koṣṇāsu sasnur munayo nadīṣu /
apām apūryanta ca nairjharīṇāṃ kuṭā girigrāmakuṭumbinībhiḥ //
jātaprakāśāsu bahiḥsthalīṣu prakāmacārotsavajāgarūkaḥ /
children.translated_text: On the outer grounds now illuminated, the elephant, jubilant in its festival of free roaming,

children.text: ibho bhuvi praskhaladagrahastaḥ sasmāra śayyodarakuñjaśayyām //
children.translated_text: stumbling with the tip of its trunk on the earth, remembered the bed of its sleeping-bower.

ibho bhuvi praskhaladagrahastaḥ sasmāra śayyodarakuñjaśayyām //

children.translated_text: Meeting their herd-companions with mutual yawning, licking off the coating of frost for a moment,

children.translated_text: the deer of the marshy meadows, surveying the circle of the horizon, set out each in their own direction.

pratasthire digvalayaṃ vilokya yathāyathaṃ kacchabhuvaḥ kuraṅgāḥ //
adṛśyatārāt taralaiḥ sthalīṣu vanecarāṇāṃ pṛtanā kuraṅgaiḥ /
children.translated_text: From afar, the restless herds of deer were seen on the plains by the forest-dwellers;

children.text: papau raveḥ saṃjvalitograbhāsaṃ bhujaṅgam aughaḥ śritanākurandhraiḥ //
children.translated_text: the mass of serpents, taking shelter in the holes of their <s>nāga</s> lairs, drank in the blazing, fierce brilliance of the sun.

children.text: adṛśyatā arāt taralaiḥ sthalīṣu vanecarāṇāṃ pṛtanā kuraṅgaiḥ /
papau raveḥ saṃjvalitograbhāsaṃ bhujaṅgam aughaḥ śritanākurandhraiḥ //
sthalaṃ kuraṅgīnayanair anidrair unmuktamudrair jalajair jalaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: The land, with the wakeful, doe-like eyes of the spotted deer, and the water, with the lotuses whose seal [of closure] was released,

children.text: vilolatārais taraladvirephair uvāha bhedaṃ na mithas tadānīm //
children.translated_text: with their trembling stars and flickering bees — bore no distinction from each other at that time.

children.text: sthalaṃ kuraṅgīnayanair anidrair unmuktamudrair jalajair jalaṃ ca /
vilolatārais taraladvirephair uvāha bhedaṃ na mithas tadānīm //
jṛmbhābharād dūravisaṃgatānāṃ mudrāvilambena dalāvalīnām /
children.translated_text: From the weight of their yawning, the petals that had parted wide, their rows of leaves loosely hanging with the release of their sealed clasp —

children.translated_text: the bee, having consumed all the pollen, departed freely from the night-lotus lakes.

children.translated_text: The sun entered the deep — it that had gone was the highest of heavenly bodies, for the highest always attains the supreme position;

children.text: āsīn mahaḥ sampadi tuṅgatāyāṃ nabho na kaiścid gadituṃ gatāyām //
children.translated_text: the splendor was at the height of its ascent to the summit of prosperity — the sky's glory, which none could describe, had risen.

children.translated_text: Detachment was assumed by the night-lotuses, which, being tranquil, [closed] slowly at the [rising of the sun's] rays;

children.translated_text: after a long time, the bees, having gathered in the abode of the day-lotuses, embraced the quality of noble companionship.

children.translated_text: The [lake] shone with the day-lotuses that displayed a rush of joy at the sight of the kinsman of lotuses [the sun];

children.translated_text: the night-lotus lake somehow bore the separation from the moon through the support of sleep.

children.text: reje 'ravindair aravindabandhoḥ saṃdarśane darśitaharṣavegaiḥ /

ūhe jalair āhitakoparāgaḥ kṣobhād alnīnāṃ nalinīparāgaḥ /
children.translated_text: The lake bore, upon its waters tinged with reddish hue, the pollen of the lotuses stirred by the agitation of the bees;

children.text: vyasarjayad dyāṃ vivṛtāparāgaḥ śaśī cirād adhyuṣitāparāgaḥ //
children.translated_text: the moon, its disk unveiled, having long inhabited the western quarter, released the sky.

children.translated_text: so too in the lake, where all the night-lotuses had closed, the red day-lotuses [blazed] all around.

children.translated_text: among the lotuses, for the swarms of bees eager for honey, there was no certainty about the entrance.

children.text: āgantave stokam api dvirephaḥ sthito dadau nāntaram abjamadhye //
children.translated_text: and standing in the midst of the lotus, did not give even the slightest room for another to approach.

children.text: luloṭha dhūlīṣu papau madhūni pakṣmāṇi līḍhāni punar lileha /
āgantave stokam api dvirephaḥ sthito dadau na antaram abjamadhye //
bheje vinidrāṃ nalinīṃ na kūlān na śīlayāmāsa navārkabhāsam /
children.translated_text: The <s>cakravāka</s> bird sought out the awakened lotus-pond, not the banks; it did not accustom itself to the new sunlight,

children.text: priyāṃ pratīyāya tathaiva mūḍhāṃ khagaḥ svabodhāgamasābhyasūyaḥ //
children.translated_text: but approached its beloved, who was still dazed — the bird resentful of the arrival of its own waking, [jealous that] she might wake too.

children.text: bheje vinidrāṃ nalinīṃ na kūlān na śīlayāmāsa navārkabhāsam /
priyāṃ pratīyāya tatha aiva mūḍhāṃ khagaḥ svabodhāgamasābhyasūyaḥ //
bahūn asau patrarathas tapasvī cakāra cāṭūn upakaṇṭhalīnaḥ /
children.translated_text: That long-suffering, leaf-winged one (<s>cakravāka</s>), clinging close to her neck, uttered many sweet flatteries,

children.text: dṛśaṃ pramīlāpagamāt kaṣāyām unmīlayāmāsa cireṇa cakrī //
children.translated_text: and after a long time made [his mate] open her eyes, reddish from the departure of drowsiness.

children.text: bahūn asau patrarathas tapasvī cakāra cāṭūn upakaṇṭhalīnaḥ /
dṛśaṃ pramīlāpagamāt kaṣāyām unmīlayāmāsa cireṇa cakrī //
pāraṃ tuṣārakṣaṇasāndhakāram api smarārtitvaritaḥ pavitrī /
children.translated_text: The <s>haṃsa</s> (swan), purifier [of waters], hastened by love's longing, though the moment of frost-darkness had passed,

children.text: śrutapriyāhnvānaravaḥ pratasthe sīmantayann abjavanaṃ vinidram //
children.translated_text: having heard the call of its beloved's name, set forth, parting the awakened lotus-grove.

children.text: pāraṃ tuṣārakṣaṇasāndhakāram api smarārtitvaritaḥ pavitrī /
śrutapriyāhnvānaravaḥ pratasthe sīmantayann abjavanaṃ vinidram //
jagāma bhañjanKamalāni kokaḥ kokīpariṣvaṅgamanorathotkaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>cakravāka</s> (male) went forth, breaking through the lotuses, eager with desire for the embrace of the <s>cakravākī</s> (female);

children.text: sāpy utsukā tatkṣaṇam ājagāma vilokayantī vanam utpalānām //
children.translated_text: she too, at that very moment, came eagerly, looking about the grove of blue lotuses.

children.text: jagāma bhañjanKamalāni kokaḥ kokīpariṣvaṅgamanorathotkaḥ /
sa āpy utsukā tatkṣaṇam ājagāma vilokayantī vanam utpalānām //
kurvāṇayoḥ sarasi padmavanāvanaddhe bhinnādhvanor vitatham eva gatāgatāni /
children.translated_text: As the two traversed different paths through the lotus-grove entwined across the lake, their comings and goings were in vain;

children.text: saṃvādidikpatitayoḥ patatoḥ kathaṃcid dvandvaṃ cirād ghaṭitam ardhapathe babhūva //
children.translated_text: falling in matching directions, the pair somehow met at last in the middle of the path.

children.text: kurvāṇayoḥ sarasi padmavanāvanaddhe bhinnādhvanor vitatham eva gatāgatāni /
saṃvādidikpatitayoḥ patatoḥ kathaṃcid dvandvaṃ cirād ghaṭitam ardhapathe babhūva //
vyasmaryatām ṛtamarīcikarābhitāpaḥ prātaḥ patatrimithunais tapanaṃ vilokya /
children.translated_text: The bird-couples, seeing the sun at dawn, forgot the torment of the heat of truthful [i.e., the sun's] rays;

children.text: jātyaiva śītalam athoṣṇam alaṃ na kiṃcic citrā gatir jagati jantudaśāvaśena //
children.translated_text: cold by nature, then hot — nothing is fixed; marvelous is the course of events in the world, subject to the condition of living beings.

children.text: vyasmaryatām ṛtamarīcikarābhitāpaḥ prātaḥ patatrimithunais tapanaṃ vilokya /
jātya aiva śītalam atha uṣṇam alaṃ na kiṃcic citrā gatir jagati jantudaśāvaśena //
kartavyanirṇayavirūḍhamanaḥprasādaśaṃsismitena mukhacandramasā virājan /
children.translated_text: Radiant with the moon of his face bearing a smile that proclaimed the serenity of mind born from the resolution of what was to be done,

children.text: rāmaḥ prabhātapavanāhitavīcikampāṃ pampām iyāya sarasīṃ saha lakṣmaṇena //
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> went to the <s>Pampā</s> lake, its waves set trembling by the morning breeze, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: kartavyanirṇayavirūḍhamanaḥprasādaśaṃsismitena mukhacandramasā virājan /
rāmaḥ prabhātapavanāhitavīcikampāṃ pampām iyāya sarasīṃ saha lakṣmaṇena //
pārśvasthāvarajasasambhramopanītapratyagrasphuṭitavilohitāravindaḥ /
children.translated_text: Accompanied by freshly blossomed red lotuses brought in eager haste by the attendant at his side,

children.text: susnātaḥ kṛtavidhir añjasopatasthe kākutsthaḥ kanakarasāvadātam arkam //
children.translated_text: having bathed well and performed the prescribed rites, <s>Kākutstha</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) straightaway worshipped the sun, radiant with a golden hue.

children.text: pārśvasthāvarajasasambhramopanītapratyagrasphuṭitavilohitāravindaḥ /
susnātaḥ kṛtavidhir añjasa ūpatasthe kākutsthaḥ kanakarasāvadātam arkam //
tau dīrghaṃ vidhivad upāsya pūrvasandhyāṃ pūṣṇīṣatprakaṭitaraśmibarbarīke /
children.translated_text: Having duly meditated at length upon the morning twilight, while the sun's rays, just revealed, formed a crest of tresses,

children.text: āsātāṃ rahitamahīruhopakaṇṭhaūdvellastimitajaṭāvanau vanānte //
children.translated_text: the two sat at the edge of the forest, near a treeless clearing, their matted locks still and upswept.

children.text: tau dīrghaṃ vidhivad upāsya pūrvasandhyāṃ pūṣṇīṣatprakaṭitaraśmibarbarīke /
āsātāṃ rahitamahīruhopakaṇṭhau udvellastimitajaṭāvanau vanānte //
ity abhinandakavikṛtau rāmacarite mahākāvye mantraviniścayapūrvakaprātaḥssandhyāvarṇano nāma tṛtīyaḥ sargaḥ samāptaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third canto, entitled 'Description of the Morning Twilight Preceded by the Deliberation of Counsel,' in the <s>Rāmacarita Mahākāvya</s> composed by the poet <s>Abhinanda</s>.
